title: Social Support and Biomarkers in Fibromyalgia Syndrome (FMS)
summary: In a previous project, we demonstrated that certain types of social support can help reduce the intensity of chronic pain in patients with complex regional pain syndrome (CRPS). To this end, the method of Ecological Momentary Assessment (EMA) was used. EMA is a method in which data on individuals’ behavior and well-being are collected in their natural everyday environments. Instead of requiring participants to come to a clinic or laboratory, they report regularly and in real time on their experiences, emotions, or symptoms during their normal daily routines. This can be done through smartphone-based questionnaires, diary entries, or other mobile technologies. The goal of EMA is to obtain more accurate and ecologically valid information about how people feel and behave compared to conventional retrospective surveys. Its main advantage is that data are collected in the natural environment and at the moment the experience occurs. Based on our EMA-derived data, we also aim to test whether and how socially supportive statements in everyday life affect fibromyalgia syndrome (FMS). To this end, we plan to conduct a so-called Ecological Momentary Intervention (EMI). We hypothesize that social contact influences pain intensity through modulation of pain perception, mediated by the autonomic nervous system, the endocrine system, and the immune system. We will investigate how individualized social interventions affect systemic and peripheral changes, the excitability of pain receptors (assessed using microneurography), and pain relief in FMS. The overarching objective is to understand how social support influences the remission or persistence of chronic pain.

interventions.name: We have followed a cohort of patients with fibromyalgia syndrome (FMS) for more than 10 years. For many participants, long-term follow-up data (≥5 years) are available. Based on changes in the Fibromyalgia Impact Questionnaire (FIQ), patients are classified as having resolved, improved, or unchanged

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients aged 18 and older with CRPS (male/female) or FMS (female). Healthy control subjects.
Exclusion criteria:
Serious other medical condition that would prevent participation in the study. For microneurography (MNG) and skin biopsy: bleeding disorder. For MNG and MRI: pacemaker or internal defibrillator, pregnant or breastfeeding women.
